Good news — as a Polish citizen you don't need a visa for a one-week trip to Hanoi.

**Primary pathway: Visa-free entry.** Poland is on Vietnam's unilateral visa-exemption list, so you can enter without applying for anything in advance.

**Key details:**
- Maximum stay: up to 45 days per visit (your week easily fits within this).
- This exemption runs through 2028-08-14 (per Resolution 229/NQ-CP).
- Your passport must be valid for at least 180 days from your entry date.
- One caveat worth flagging: the policy data notes this exemption is specifically tied to "tourism purpose." Since you're traveling for business meetings, it's worth double-checking with the Vietnamese embassy/consulate or evisa.gov.vn that business meetings fall within the activities allowed under visa-free entry (general business meetings are usually fine, but formal work/labor activities are not). If you want a document that unambiguously covers business travel, see the e-Visa option below.

**Fallback option — e-Visa:** If you'd rather not rely on the tourism-purpose exemption, an e-Visa is available to all nationalities, allows stays up to 90 days, costs USD 25 (single-entry) or USD 50 (multiple-entry), and takes about 2-3 business days to process at evisa.gov.vn.

**One more thing:** This data is current as of 2026-08-17. Since policies can change, I'd recommend a quick check at https://evisa.gov.vn/ before you fly, especially to confirm the tourism-vs-business distinction for your specific meetings.
